title: Operational sim lab: steward checklist & failure rehearsals (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for an operational simulation lab tailored to release stewards. Goal: provide a compact checklist + scripted failure rehearsals that any steward can run pre-canary and during early exposure windows. Focus is on cross-functional choreography (product, SRE, infra, observability, CX) and making human decisions predictable.

Scope:
- Applies to medium-to-high risk LLM rollouts (model or routing changes, cost gating, or quality regressions).
- Not a replacement for the full canary runbook; this is the steward-facing playbook for rehearsal and early detection.
- Includes: pre-sim checklist, three scripted failure scenarios, telemetry queries to run, quick rollback and mitigation activations, and a short postmortem template.

Quick TL;DR for a steward (one-pager):
- 60m sim window before live canary kickoff. Invite: product PM, steward, SRE on-call, obs engineer, solutions engineer.
- Run baseline traffic capture, inject synthetic cohort (5% traffic slice), run scenario A (latency spike), scenario B (model quality drift), scenario C (fallback cascade).
- Verify alerts fire and run manual decision flow. If any step fails, abort canary.

Roles and ownership (practical):
- Steward (you): run the checklist, hold the timeline, call abort or proceed.
- Product PM: hypothesis owner, acceptance metrics (quality delta thresholds).
- SRE (on-call): executes traffic shaping, can toggle routing and capacity limits.
- Observability eng: pre-creates queries and alert bindings; makes dashboards visible.
- CX/Support rep: reads the incident comms template and stands ready to triage incoming tickets.

Pre-sim checklist (run in order):
1) Confirm hypothesis + guardrails: product PM states one-sentence hypothesis and three acceptance criteria.
2) Baseline snapshot (take perf & quality): run baseline queries (list below) and capture CPU/GPU utilization for last 1h.
3) Canary slice defined: cohort id, percentage, user flags, sampling key. Ensure slice orthogonality (no overlap with other experiments).
4) Alert bindings: ensure all alert channels mapped (PagerDuty, Slack #canary-watch, email).
5) Rollback & escape hatches: verify route toggle runbook link, model-pin endpoint ready, traffic kill switch verified by SRE.
6) Communication: scheduled timing message posted in #release-orchestra and stakeholders invited to 60m sim.

Telemetry & baseline queries (cut-and-paste friendly):
- latency_p95(route:service) last_1h
- token_cost_per_request(model:variant) last_1h
- users_with_errors_5xx last_1h
- rerank_precision@10(prompt_class) baseline vs current
- prompt_prefix_cache_hit_rate last_1h
(Obs eng: please save as dashboard tile ‘sim-lab baseline’).

Sim scenarios (scripted):
Scenario A — Latency spike (purpose: test SLA & autoscale):
- Setup: increase per-model simulated request size / pause batcher thread on a staging node (SRE action).
- Expected: p95 latency alert at 2x baseline within 5m, fallback routing to warm model variant triggers, no more than 3% request failures for 10m.
- Steward actions: if routing fallback reduces latency within 10m, continue; if not, abort and revert traffic.

Scenario B — Model quality drift (purpose: detect regressive outputs):
- Setup: swap in a slightly older model variant or synthetic prompt set that produces known failure mode.
- Signals: drop in rerank_precision@10 by >5 points, increase in negative-sentiment rate for targeted prompts, surge in manual review flags.
- Steward actions: hold, escalate to product owner; if acceptance metrics breached, pin previous model and stop canary traffic.

Scenario C — Fallback cascade & cost surge (purpose: validate cost-awareness and escape hatch):
- Setup: force cache-miss pattern (randomize prefixes) and trigger a synthetic traffic spike (SRE injects) to simulate cache cold-start + burst.
- Signals: token_cost_per_request jumps >1.8x, billing burn-rate alert, autoscaler schedules more nodes but queue latency increases.
- Steward actions: activate cost thermostat (reduce batch size, route to cheaper quantized variant) or trigger emergency capacity cap; if cost still grows, abort.

Decision matrix (simplified):
- Critical (safety, data leakage, security): immediate abort + page security response.
- High (quality regression > threshold, sustained p95 breach >15m): abort and revert model.
- Medium (transient latency blip <10m, single metric spike): engage mitigation (fallback variant) and continue monitoring.
- Low (minor telemetry noise): note in decision log and proceed.

Run log / artifact collection (must attach to canary run):
- baseline snapshot (filename)
- sim config (traffic seed, cohort ids)
- timeline of events (minute granularity)
- screenshots of dashboard panels
- decision log: timestamped actions (proceed/hold/abort) + rationale

Communications templates (short):
- Pre-sim announcement: "Sim lab scheduled at HH:MM. Steward: <name>. Expected duration 60m. If abort, we'll withdraw canary and update."
- Abort message: "Abort: canary suspended. Reason: <one-line>. Next steps: <rollback steps>. Notifying: SRE, product, CX."

Post-sim short postmortem (fields):
- what we tested (scenarios)
- top signals observed (list)
- steward decisions and timestamps
- root cause hypothesis (if any)
- action items (owner + due date)

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- How to safely run scenario B with live user PII? Need stubbed prompt sets or synthetic prompts. (owner: Priya)
- Can we automate scenario A with a service-level fault injector instead of manual SRE steps? (owner: Marco)
- Tie the sim-lab report to rollout tickets automatically (small webhook). (owner: Dmitri)

Quick friction notes (lessons from last run):
- Observability bindings were not pre-created; obs eng had to scramble to expose a rare metric (cost per token). Fix: pre-create dashboard tiles for common sims.
- SRE runway for capacity toggles needs a dry-run script and a readback confirmation step.

Appendix: minimal queries (copy-ready)
- baseline_latency_p95 = query("p95(latency) by route")
- baseline_quality = query("rerank_precision@10 where prompt_class=in(['search','summarize'])")
- cost_probe = query("sum(token_cost) by model_variant over 10m")

Decision log template (one-line entries):
- 2025-09-03T14:02Z | steward=Lena Zhao | action=simulate-start | note=baseline captured
- 2025-09-03T14:12Z | steward=Lena Zhao | action=scenario-A-injected | note=observed p95=1.9s
- 2025-09-03T14:22Z | steward=Lena Zhao | action=fallback-activated | note=p95->0.6s

Notes to self (informal):
- Need a small wrapper script to toggle model pin and route; SSHing into infra is too slow.
- Consider a "sim-lab" toggle in Console to create ephemeral slices and isolate logs.

References / links (keep these handy):
- Canaries runbook (stable): confluence:/release/canary-runbook (link above)
- Model pin API: https://api.redwood.example/docs/model-pin
- PagerDuty schedule: SRE-oncall rotation

End (draft). This is deliberately terse — the goal is a small checklist the steward can run without paging half the company. Feedback welcome: add small automations, reduce manual SRE steps, and harden the cost thermostat triggers.
